append.text: **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:2) *dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis* → *conduzis aos infernos, e trazeis de volta*** — the Latin's plural kept as the Portuguese plural *os infernos*, the traditional term for the realm of the dead; *trazeis de volta* in the same line tells the listener it is a place one returns from. The ambiguity reader still heard 'send to hell'. The Brazilian Creed says *desceu à mansão dos mortos* (`ps212/circulation.md`); the CNBB LH paraphrases this line *fazeis descer aos abismos da terra*. See the proposed formula row *ad ínferos* (212, 223, 234) — for Gustavo.

**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:2) the verb *flagelláre* (*tu flagéllas, et salvas*) → *flagelais*** — the noun's family, kept apart from *castigáre → castigar* four verses on (13:6); see the *flagelláre* row.

**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:5) *álius Deus omnípotens præter eum* → *outro Deus todo-poderoso senão ele*** (the Creed's *Pai todo-poderoso*, fetched again, `ps212/circulation.md`); *onipotente* kept as the option. No reader remarked.

**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:2) *et redúcis* (no *íterum*) → *e trazeis de volta*** — the row's verb, with *de volta* for the re- as 70:20 had *de novo*; *fazeis voltar* and *reconduzis* are options. The CNBB LH has *trazeis novamente* in the same line.

**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:4) *ídeo … ut* (forward-pointing) → *para isto … para que*** (v2): a local departure. v1's cleft *foi por isso que* was heard pointing back by the ambiguity reader and found heavy by the stylist; *por isso* stays the row's word where ídeo points back (30:23b). Passed the v2 gate.
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:4) *ut vos enarrétis mirabília ejus* → *para que narreis vós as suas maravilhas*** (the Latin's *vos* kept after the verb, the stylist's order).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:7) *Aspícite ergo quæ fecit nobíscum* → *Olhai, pois, o que ele fez conosco*** (the row's verb with a clause object).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:11) *omnes elécti ejus* → *todos os seus escolhidos*** — the CNBB LH and Lectionary have *seus eleitos* in the same line (`ps212/circulation.md`); the row's word kept.
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:11) *ágite dies lætítiæ* → *celebrai dias de alegria*** (the row's verb; MS1932 and DRB the same).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:8) *in terra captivitátis meæ* → *na terra do meu cativeiro*** (the CNBB LH the same).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:7) *cum timóre et tremóre confitémini illi* → *com temor e tremor dai-lhe graças*** (the pair and rhyme kept).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:6) twice: *por causa das nossas iniquidades … por causa da sua misericórdia*** (6:5's wording).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:3, 7, 8, 11) → *dai graças*, *dai-lhe graças*, *lhe darei graças*** — four times, the canticle's spine.
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:11) *Benedícite Dóminum, omnes elécti ejus* → *Bendizei o Senhor, todos os seus escolhidos*** (accusative, as 133:1a).

**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:7, 13:9)**: *quæ fecit nobíscum* → *o que ele fez conosco* (125:3); *fáciat vobíscum misericórdiam suam* → *usará da sua misericórdia convosco* (17:51's idiom; the stylist's order). *tratar* does not fit either: the object is a clause or *misericórdia*.
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:4) of people: *dispérsit vos inter gentes* → *vos dispersou entre as nações*** (43:12's build).
**Canticle 212 (Tob 13:6) *Ipse castigávit nos* → *Ele nos castigou*** (kept apart from *flagelláre* in 13:2).

terms: | flagelláre | flagelar (*Porque vós flagelais, e salvais*) | open | **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:2)**; not a psalter verb (the noun is, D39). Kept apart from *castigáre → castigar* (13:6, 117:18); MS1932 *castigas* and the CNBB LH *castigais* merge them. The ambiguity reader listed *flagelais* as a word a listener may not know, and heard it as scourging; kept as the Latin's image. |

| effúgere (*manum tuam*) | escapar de (*e não há quem escape da vossa mão*) | open | **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:2)**; not a psalter word. The Brazilian regency *escapar de*; the CNBB LH has *de vossa mão nada pode escapar*. |

| ignoráre (a person) | *não conhecer* (*as nações, que não o conhecem*) | open | **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:4) *gentes, quæ ignórant eum***. *ignorar alguém* is heard in Brazil as 'snub'; DRB 'know not', MS1932 *que o não conhecem*. The cost: 78:6 *quæ te non novérunt* → *que não vos conhecem* has another Latin verb. 34:15 *et ignorávi → e eu não soube* (no object). The Latinist asked for the comma (descriptive clause), taken. |

| Rex sæculórum | o Rei dos séculos (*e exaltai o Rei dos séculos nas vossas obras*) | open | **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:7)**, and DO's antiphon for the canticle *Exaltáte Regem sæculórum in opéribus vestris* (Psalmi major). sæcula as 144:13a *de todos os séculos*, not the D23 formula; the CNBB LH has *o Rei sempiterno*. The ambiguity reader heard 'eternal King'. |

| præter (after a negation) | senão (*que não há outro Deus todo-poderoso senão ele*) | open | 17:32 *quis Deus præter Dóminum? → quem é Deus senão o Senhor?*; **Canticle 212 (Tob 13:5)**, MS1932 the same. *além dele* (DRB 'besides', the CNBB LH) is the option. |
formulas: | *ad ínferos* — *dedúcis ad ínferos, et redúcis* (canticle 212, Tob 13:2) · *dedúcit ad ínferos et redúcit* (canticle 223, 1 Sam 2:9 in DO's ids) · *descéndit ad ínferos* (canticle 234, the Athanasian Creed) | *aos infernos* (212: *conduzis aos infernos, e trazeis de volta*); 223 and 234 to follow | open — **for Gustavo.** Proposed by canticle 212: the Latin's plural as the Portuguese plural, the older term for the realm of the dead, one with the psalter's *inferno* for *inférnus*. Against it: the Brazilian Creed now says *desceu à mansão dos mortos*, and the CNBB LH paraphrases 212's line *aos abismos da terra*; the 212 ambiguity reader heard 'send to hell'. Alternatives: *à morada dos mortos* / *à mansão dos mortos* (the Creed's, and for 234 the obvious one), *ao inferno* (the row's singular). |
